items.informal_name: Sum of Negated Finite Support Function
items.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {M : Type u_8} {G : Type u_12} [inst : SubtractionMonoid G] [inst_1 : AddCommMonoid M] {g : α →₀ G}
  {h : α → G → M}, (∀ (a : α), h a 0 = 0) → (-g).sum h = g.sum fun a b => h a (-b)
items.informal_description: For any finite support function $ g : \alpha \to G $ where $ G $ is a subtraction monoid and $ M $ is an additive commutative monoid, and for any function $ h : \alpha \to G \to M $ satisfying $ h(a, 0) = 0 $ for all $ a $, the sum of $ h(a, -g(a)) $ over $ \alpha $ equals the sum of $ h(a, -b) $ over the support of $ g $. This establishes that negating a finite support function and summing with $ h $ is equivalent to summing the original function with $ h $ applied to negated values.

items.informal_name: Negation of Sum Equals Sum of Negations for Dependent Finite Support Functions
items.informal_description: For any dependent finite support function $ g $ from an index type $ \iota $ to a family of additive groups $ \beta(i) $, and for any function $ h $ mapping each index $ i $ and value $ b $ to an additive commutative monoid $ \gamma $ such that $ h(i, 0) = 0 $ for all $ i $, the sum of $ h $ over the negated function $ -g $ equals the sum of $ h(i, -b) $ over the support of $ g $.

items.informal_description: For any finite support function $ f : \alpha \to₀ M $ and function $ h : \alpha \to M \to G $ where $ G $ is an additive commutative group, the sum of $ -h(a, b) $ over $ f $ equals the negation of the sum of $ h(a, b) $ over $ f $. Formally, $ \sum_{a \in \text{support}(f)} -h(a, f(a)) = -\sum_{a \in \text{support}(f)} h(a, f(a)) $.

Formally, $ \sum_{i \in \text{supp}(f)} -h(i, f(i)) = -\sum_{i \in \text{supp}(f)} h(i, f(i)) $.

  (s : Finset ι) (f : ι → α), ∑ i ∈ -s, f i = ∑ i ∈ s, f (-i)
items.informal_description: For any finite set $ s $ over a type $ \iota $ with involutive negation and a function $ f : \iota \to \alpha $ where $ \alpha $ is an additive commutative monoid, the sum of $ f(i) $ over the negated set $ -s $ is equal to the sum of $ f(-i) $ over the original set $ s $. Formally, $ \sum_{i \in -s} f(i) = \sum_{i \in s} f(-i) $.

items.informal_name: Product identity for a negated function with finite support
items.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {M : Type u_8} {G : Type u_12} [inst : SubtractionMonoid G] [inst_1 : CommMonoid M] {g : α →₀ G}
  {h : α → G → M}, (∀ (a : α), h a 0 = 1) → (-g).prod h = g.prod fun a b => h a (-b)
items.informal_description:
Let $G$ be a subtraction monoid and $M$ be a commutative monoid. Let $g$ be a function from a type $\alpha$ to $G$ with finite support. Let $h$ be a function that maps an element $a \in \alpha$ and an element $b \in G$ to an element $h(a, b) \in M$, such that for all $a \in \alpha$, $h(a, 0) = 1$. Then the product associated with the pointwise negation of $g$ is given by the formula:
$$ \prod_{a \in \text{supp}(-g)} h(a, (-g)(a)) = \prod_{a \in \text{supp}(g)} h(a, -(g(a))) $$
Here, $\text{supp}(f)$ denotes the support of a function $f$ (the set of points where it is non-zero), and $(-g)(a) = -(g(a))$.
